result.title: February 7, 2025
result.summary: LACERS RFP No. 4282 seeks actuarial consulting services. Released January 24, 2025, proposals are due electronically February 21, 2025. Julie Guan is the RFP Administrator. Written questions are due by February 7 and must be sent to her; questions and answers, and any official addenda, will be posted on the LACERS website. Proposers are responsible for monitoring the site and following addenda. From release until contract execution, firms may communicate about the RFP only with the Administrator; prohibited contact with Board members or other staff may result in disqualification under LACERS’ ethics policy. The RFP covers introduction, minimum qualifications, consulting/advisory and as-needed services, response contents (introduction, qualifications and experience, project proposal, and actuary fee schedule), submission instructions and evaluation, general conditions and compliance documents, and Executive Directive 35.

result.title: I. INTRODUCTION
result.summary: LACERS seeks proposals from qualified public-pension actuarial consultants meeting Section II qualifications. It plans a full-service three-year Consulting Actuary contract, with up to two one-year extensions. The consultant must serve LACERS and its members exclusively, may serve the City only at LACERS’ request, and must cooperate with any City-appointed actuary or auditor by supplying requested data. Established in 1937, LACERS covers about 25,200 active employees and 22,500 retirees and beneficiaries, paying roughly $1.21 billion in pensions and $174 million in retiree-health premiums annually. Its seven-member Board governs the system; benefits are set by the City, with Tier 1 (including Enhanced) and Tier 3 memberships. LACERS administers a defined-benefit retirement plan, postemployment health plan (401(h) and 115 Trust), Larger Annuity Plan, and Family Death Benefit Plan. The RFP directs proposers to online valuations, audits, studies, policies, financial reports, and Board materials and lists relevant meeting dates. A separate future RFP may select an Audit Actuary to review assumptions and validate valuations.

result.title: II. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
result.summary: Firms must demonstrate these minimum qualifications to be considered: at least five years providing comparable actuarial consulting services to U.S. public pension funds; a supervising/lead actuary with at least 15 years’ experience with major public employee retirement systems, including three years serving California public pension clients similar to LACERS in size and services. The lead actuary must meet American Academy of Actuaries qualification standards, hold an SOA Fellow or Associate designation or equivalent, directly supervise all LACERS services, and be an employee regularly engaged in actuarial services. Every actuary performing the work must meet Academy standards. The lead actuary should explain actuarial theory, assumptions, and other actuarial matters in readily understood language.

result.title: III. SCOPE OF SERVICES
key_items: 20. COST ANALYSIS FOR BENEFIT CHANGES; 21. FUNDING POLICY REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATION; 22. INDIVIDUAL BENEFIT CALCULATIONS
result.summary: The scope covers actuarial advice and timely access by phone, video, email, writing, or in person; Board and public-body presentations/testimony; funding and benefit recommendations; regulatory updates; and review of data quality. Annual retirement and health-subsidy valuations, gain/loss analyses, assumptions, contribution rates, disclosures, and reports are required, alongside ASOP 51 risk assessments with deterministic and stochastic projections. It includes biennial Larger Annuity Program and Family Death Benefit Plan asset/liability studies, a triennial experience study, GASB and AICPA reporting, ACFR valuation material, annual CPI/COLA determinations and COLA-bank schedules, and assumption confirmation letters. As-needed work includes education and symposium presentations; member-benefit tools and calculations; collaboration with auditors, consultants, vendors, and other professionals; cost analyses of proposed changes; funding-policy review; complex individual-benefit reviews; and other actuarial, asset-liability, allocation, plan-design, risk, UAAL, system-calculation, and cash-flow studies.

result.title: B. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
result.summary: The RFP requests evidence of minimum qualifications: descriptions of similar public pension contracts from the past five years, including services, client/address, dates, fees, and reference contact details; submission permits LACERS to contact references. Provide the lead actuary’s and all participating actuaries’ resumes, covering titles, relevant experience and years, credentials, specified current and past public pension clients (including California clients for the lead), and engagement roles. The firm must answer each company question in its proposal: history, founding year, entity type, locations, services, staffing and credentials, ownership and changes; quality assurance and calculation checks; hardware/software; clients lost in five years; independence and conflicts; requested liability limits; E&O insurance; legal actions; keeping current with regulations and actuarial standards; recent public-sector pro bono work; client-data protection and breaches; privacy policies and facility/access controls; a recent SOC report or security audit; and a sample proposed contract.

result.title: C. PROJECT PROPOSAL
result.summary: The project proposal must show the firm’s understanding and approach by repeating each question and providing a response. It must describe the overall work and transition from LACERS’ prior actuary; collaboration on actuarial methods and assumptions, data reasonableness review, and corrections; resolving ambiguity in plan terms; milestone timelines and deadlines; required data and formats; safeguards for Social Security numbers and other private information; communication of compliance and regulatory policies; staff support needed; and transition to a successor actuary if the contract ends. Include sample retirement and health valuations, experience study, risk assessment, and benefit-change cost study for a comparable client; explain the firm’s value-add; suggest 30–60-minute Pension Symposium topics for Board members, staff, and the public; and provide any additional information.

result.title: D. PROPOSED CONSULTING ACTUARY FEE SCHEDULE
key_items: PROJECT FEE FOR SERVICE – AS NEEDED
result.summary: Requires a detailed consulting actuary fee proposal by year (Years 1–5), including an annual retainer for the listed consulting/advisory services and reasonable unlimited client questions with follow-up. Price required studies and valuations: annual retirement-benefit valuation/GASB 67; OPEB valuation/GASB 74; risk assessment; alternating-year assets-and-liabilities studies for the Larger Annuity Program (even years) and Family Death Benefit Insurance Plan (odd years); triennial experience study; employer GASB 68 and GASB 75 reporting; ACFR valuation summary; and annual retiree COLA analysis. Specify Board presentations and whether risk assessment is included in valuation fees. Project fees must cover draft and final work, follow-up, and indicated presentations; travel is priced separately. Provide not-to-exceed fees for as-needed Board Actuarial 101, LACERS Pension Symposium, and funding-policy review services; hourly rates by personnel class for approved ad-hoc work; and inclusive travel rates for the first and each additional presentation day. Proposers may suggest cost-saving alternative pricing.

result.title: V. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & EVALUATION
key_items: e. Level V – Final Approval by the Board; Date
e. Level V – Final Approval by the Board
result.summary: Proposals must be submitted electronically by the cover-sheet deadline, labeled with the firm name and “Proposal for Consulting Actuary Engagement.” LACERS may retain responses as public records; proposers claiming confidential or proprietary material must also provide a separately redacted copy and agree to defend and indemnify LACERS against disclosure-related claims, or waive the exemption. Board/Committee presenters may be asked for 10 hard copies. Questions and all RFP communications must be in writing to the named administrator. LACERS may treat a single response as failed competition or award sole-source, select multiple firms, verify submissions, reject false information, withdraw or reject responses, extend deadlines, and makes no award guarantee. Evaluation has five stages: administrative responsiveness and contract terms; qualifications, experience, references, and due diligence; video interview; services and compensation; and Board approval. Scoring: professionalism 15%, scope/methodology 30%, qualifications/experience/accomplishments 35%, and cost/value 20%. The tentative schedule runs from RFP release Jan. 24, 2025, through questions, responses, Feb. 21 proposal deadline, evaluation, interviews, and anticipated Apr. 8 Board recommendation; dates may change.

result.title: Contract Compliance and Executive Directive 35
key_items: VI. GENERAL CONDITIONS AND COMPLIANCE DOCUMENTS
result.summary: Proposers must submit the documents required by Appendix A, which cover standard LACERS and City of Los Angeles contract provisions and may involve added costs, including insurance and business tax registration. This is a new contract, so previous submissions or waivers do not apply and new forms must be completed. Under Executive Directive 35, awarded for-profit contractors must report their and their subcontractors’ revenue, employee count, location, industry, and majority owner’s race/ethnicity and gender through RAMP within 30 days of the contract start and annually thereafter. Contractors must also ask subcontractors to update their RAMP business profiles annually. These disclosures are informational and do not affect bidding, selection, or award.
